rules: When the current privilege mode is enabled for recording and the transfer type is not inhibited and sctrstatus .FROZEN is not set, a control transfer is qualified.
Qualified control transfers update the Entry Registers at logical entry 0.
If the CTR buffer is full, the oldest recorded entry is lost.
Recorded transfers set the ctrsource .V bit to 1 and update all implemented record fields.
The SCTRCLR instruction zeroes all CTR Entry Registers, the CTR cycle counter, and the Cycle Count Valid (CCV) bit.
SCTRCLR raises an illegal-instruction exception in U-mode, and a virtual-instruction exception in VUmode, unless CTR state enable access restrictions apply.

When mstateen0 .CTR is 0 and the privilege mode is less privileged than M-mode, attempts to access sctrctl, vsctrctl, sctrdepth, sctrstatus, sireg* when siselect is in 0x200..0x2FF, or vsireg* when vsiselect is in 0x200..0x2FF, or execution of the SCTRCLR instruction raise an illegal-instruction exception.
When mstateen0 .CTR is 1 and hstateen0 .CTR is 1, VS-mode accesses to supervisor CTR state behave as described in Section 7.2 and Section 11.2.
When mstateen0 .CTR is 1 and hstateen0 .CTR is 0, VS-mode accesses to supervisor CTR state and VSmode execution of SCTRCLR raise a virtual-instruction exception.
If the H extension is implemented, when mstateen0 .CTR is 1 and hstateen0 .CTR is 1, hstateen0 .CTR controls access to supervisor CTR state when V=1.
When sctrstatus .FROZEN is set, transfer recording is inhibited.
When sctrctl .LCOFIFRZ is 1 and a local-counter-overflow interrupt traps to M-mode or to S-mode, sctrstatus .FROZEN is set by hardware.
When sctrctl .BPFRZ is 1 and a breakpoint exception traps to M-mode or S-mode, sctrstatus .FROZEN is set by hardware.
When the H extension is implemented, freeze behavior for LCOFIs and breakpoint exceptions that trap to VSmode is determined by the LCOFIFRZ and BPFRZ values in vsctrctl.
When an external trap is recorded, the ctrtarget .PC is 0.
External trap recording depends on the external trap enable bits for the target mode and all intervening modes being enabled for recording.
When an external trap is recorded, the ctrtarget .PC is 0.
If an external trap is recorded, the ctrtarget .PC is 0.
If sctrctl .STE is set, U-mode can opt-in to record traps to S-mode.
If mctrctl .MTE and sctrctl .STE are implemented, U-mode can opt-in to record external traps to M-mode.
If mctrctl .MTE, sctrctl .STE, and vsctrctl .STE are implemented, VS-mode can opt-in to record external traps to M-mode.
When mstateen0 .CTR is 0 and the privilege mode is less privileged than M-mode, attempts to access sireg* when siselect is in 0x200..0x2FF raise an illegal-instruction exception.
When mstateen0 .CTR is 0 and the privilege mode is less privileged than M-mode, attempts to access vsireg* when vsiselect is in 0x200..0x2FF raise an illegal-instruction exception.

When siselect holds a value in the range 0x40-0x5F and a counter i is delegated (mcounteren [ i ]=1 and menvcfg .CDE=1), the register state associated with counter i can be read or written via sireg*, while siselect holds 0x40+ i.

If any extension upon which the underlying state for a specific siselect and sireg* combination depends is not implemented, an attempt from M or S mode to access the given state through sireg* raises an illegal-instruction exception.

If any extension upon which the underlying state for a specific siselect and sireg* combination depends is not implemented, an attempt from M or S mode to access the given state through sireg* raises an illegal-instruction exception.

If the H extension is implemented, attempts from VS-mode to access any sireg* (really vsireg*) raises an illegal-instruction exception if menvcfg .CDE = 0, or a virtual-instruction exception if menvcfg .CDE = 1.
If an implementation of any transfer type filter bit results in reduced software performance, it is recommended that this reduced performance applies only when the bit is set.
When CtrCycleCounter is incremented, the CC field is encoded such that CCE holds 0 if the CtrCycleCounter value is less than 4096.
The elapsed cycle count can be calculated by software using the formula if (CCE==0): return CCM else: return (2 12 + CCM) << CCE-1 endif.
The CtrCycleCounter is reset on writes to x ctrctl, and on execution of SCTRCLR.
Attempts to access sctrdepth from VS-mode or VU-mode raise a virtual-instruction exception, unless CTR state enable access restrictions apply.
